---
title: "Sex Differences Along a Microglia Trajectory in DLPFC (IPRE, Winter 2026)"
description: "Trajectory inference from homeostatic to disease-associated microglia in SEA-AD prefrontal cortex, with tradeSeq tests for sex differences along pseudotime."
---

- **Student:** Cristóbal Herrera (IPRE, Winter 2026)
- **Supervisor:** Tomás González Zarzar
- **Data:** [SEA-AD](../databases/sea-ad.qmd) snRNA-seq, dorsolateral
  prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), microglia
- **Status:** finished as an IPRE project. Exploratory; see
  [Caveats](#caveats) before using any of it.

## The question

Microglia move from a homeostatic state toward a disease-associated state
(DAM) in Alzheimer's disease. Do they do so differently in men and women?

Microglia were chosen as the brain's resident immune cells, well represented
in the dataset, with the focus on inflammatory mechanisms. The DLPFC was
chosen because it is among the cortical regions reported to differ most
between sexes in Alzheimer's disease, and it accumulates amyloid early.

## What was done

The project extends the trajectory tutorial (03b) of the lab's
[single-cell tutorials](https://omnia-lab-uc.github.io/single-cell_tutorials/)
from one donor and one lineage to microglia from the whole DLPFC cohort, and
runs the `tradeSeq` analysis that the tutorial leaves as an optional exercise.

1. **Loading.** Donor files were downloaded with `aws s3 sync` from
   `PFC/RNAseq/donors_objects` and read with `zellkonverter` and `HDF5Array`,
   which keep the matrices on disk. Each donor was subset to microglia in a
   loop.
2. **Quality control.** QC metrics were computed with `scrapper`. Adaptive
   thresholds were compared with the fixed thresholds from the tutorial and
   kept, leaving 34,828 nuclei and discarding 5,971.
3. **Preprocessing.** `scran` pooling normalization, 2,000 highly variable
   genes, PCA, and UMAP.
4. **Clustering.** For the trajectory, 1,500 highly variable genes gave
   cleaner clusters than 2,000. PCA with 50 components, UMAP on the first 20,
   and graph clustering on the PCA (k = 20, Louvain) gave 11 clusters.
5. **Trajectory.** Each cluster was scored for homeostatic and DAM marker
   genes. Cluster 3 (high homeostatic, low DAM) was set as the start and
   cluster 11 (high DAM) as the end. `slingshot` returned six lineages;
   lineage 1 runs from cluster 3 to cluster 11 and was taken as the trajectory
   of interest. It leaves 12,559 nuclei outside, in clusters that are not on
   that path.
6. **Check against pathology.** Pseudotime along lineage 1 was compared
   between donors grouped by Braak stage, Thal phase, and overall AD
   neuropathological change.
7. **Differential expression along pseudotime.** `tradeSeq::fitGAM()` on raw
   counts for the 1,500 genes, with seven knots, sex as the condition, and
   highest education level as a covariate. Then `associationTest()` for genes
   that change along lineage 1 in at least one sex, and `conditionTest()` with
   a log2 fold change threshold of 0.5 for genes whose pattern differs between
   sexes. Both at FDR < 0.05.

![UMAP of microglia with the lineage 1 curve. Orange: the start cluster
(homeostatic). Red: the end cluster (DAM).](images/microglia-trajectory-umap.png)

## What came out

**The pseudotime does not follow pathology.** If lineage 1 captured disease
progression, donors at later stages should sit further along it. They don't:
the distributions overlap and are multimodal at every stage, for Braak, Thal,
and overall AD change alike.

![Distribution of pseudotime along lineage 1, by donor Braak stage. There is
no ordering by stage.](images/microglia-trajectory-braak.png)

**Genes along the trajectory.** 719 of the 1,500 genes change along lineage 1
in at least one sex. Of those, 29 also differ between sexes:

| Group | Genes |
|---|---|
| Sex-chromosome genes | *TSIX*, *NLGN4Y*, *TTTY14*, *LINC00278* (Y-linked or X-inactivation), *CYBB*, *TMSB4X* (X-linked) |
| Microglial activation, lipid, iron, and stress response | *MS4A6A*, *PLIN2*, *FTL*, *SIGLEC1*, *MT2A*, *NUPR1*, *HSPB1*, *SERPINB9* |
| Interferon response | *IFI44L*, *MX2* |
| Other | *IGSF21*, *ERC2*, *ARHGAP31*, *ANKUB1*, *KCNIP4*, *PHACTR1*, *ADGRB3*, *ANKRD22*, *MALAT1*, *RPL35*, *RPS15*, *AC120193.1*, *AC011933.4* |

Cristóbal singled out *MS4A6A* (modulates TREM2 signaling), *PLIN2* (a marker
of lipid-droplet-accumulating microglia), *FTL* (iron storage), and *CYBB*
(NADPH oxidase) as the most interpretable. *PLIN2* rises toward the end of
the trajectory more in males.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Fitted expression of the 29 genes along lineage 1, female
donors.](images/microglia-trajectory-heatmap-female.png)

![The same, male donors. Rows are clustered separately in each panel, so the
gene order differs.](images/microglia-trajectory-heatmap-male.png)
:::

His own conclusion is the right one: the gene list is only as meaningful as
the trajectory under it, and it is unclear what this trajectory captures. The
background on DAM as a conserved microglial state is in
[Cheng & Ho (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3003426).

## Caveats {#caveats}

- **The trajectory is not validated.** It was built from marker genes
  described in mouse models and does not track any of the donor-level
  pathology measures. Genes that rise at the end of pseudotime are also
  expressed in nuclei off the trajectory.
- **Nuclei were treated as independent samples.** Sex is a property of the
  donor, but `tradeSeq` fits one model across all nuclei and does not know
  which donor each came from. Thousands of nuclei from a few dozen donors
  make differences look far more certain than they are. This is the
  pseudoreplication problem described in tutorial 03a, and it is the main
  reason not to trust the 29 genes as they stand.
- **Several hits are sex-chromosome genes**, which differ between sexes in
  every cell type and say nothing about the trajectory.
- **Some genes look like they come from other cells.** *ERC2*, *KCNIP4*, and
  *ADGRB3* are neuronal genes; in microglia nuclei they are more likely
  ambient RNA than microglial expression. Not checked.
- **Only one covariate.** `fitGAM()` on 1,500 genes took about nine hours on
  a laptop, so only education level was adjusted for. Age, post-mortem
  interval, and comorbidities were planned and not run. The number of knots
  was set to seven without running `evaluateK()`, for the same reason.
- **Donors were not integrated.** Clusters, and so the trajectory, can
  reflect differences between donors as well as cell states.
- **Not reproducible yet.** Only the `tradeSeq` script was archived. The
  loading, QC, clustering, and `slingshot` code exists only as slides.

## Next steps

If you pick this up:

1. Decide first whether there is a trajectory worth testing. Integrate the
   donors, rebuild it, and check it against pathology again. A pseudotime that
   doesn't order donors by any measure of disease is not a disease axis.
2. Compare with the microglial states SEA-AD already annotated (the
   `Supertype` column) before defining new clusters.
3. Make the donor the unit of analysis. For example, split pseudotime into a
   few bins, sum counts per donor within each bin, and test sex and its
   interaction with the bin using the pseudobulk approach from tutorial 04.
4. Keep `tradeSeq` for exploration, on a subsample of nuclei or on the
   cluster, where trying different covariates and `evaluateK()` is feasible.
5. Remove the sex-chromosome genes from any list before interpreting it.
